problem: "Some syllabi call the resulting device a Mach-Zehnder modulator (MZM)" makes the standard name sound like an optional local usage. A student may think MZM is a non-standard alias.
fix: "The device that turns the phase change into an intensity change is the Mach-Zehnder modulator (MZM); this is its standard name."

where: Section 1, Vπ definition, and Quiz Q1
problem: The text defines Vπ as "the voltage that gives a phase shift of π radians", but Q1 defines it as the voltage that gives a phase difference of π between the two arms. In push-pull drive each arm only shifts π/2 when V = Vπ, so the two wordings disagree by a factor of two and can lead a student to double the arm phase.
fix: Define Vπ once as: the voltage that makes the phase difference between the two arms equal π radians (the voltage that moves the output from maximum to the first null). Keep the same wording in Q1.

problem: The sentence "The modulator works by the electro-optic or Pockels effect" is written for all external modulators, yet Section 3 describes the EAM, which works by field-induced absorption, not the Pockels effect. A student may assume every external modulator uses the Pockels effect.
fix: "The Mach-Zehnder modulator works by the electro-optic (Pockels) effect: an electric field E changes the refractive index n of a material without inversion symmetry, such as lithium niobate (LiNbO3) or indium phosphide (InP)."

problem: The travelling-wave electrode point (electrical and optical waves travel together, low drive voltage at high bit rates) is stated in full twice, once in Section 3 and again in Beyond.
fix: Keep the explanation in Section 3 and let Beyond add only the new material (silicon photonics, thin-film lithium niobate, EML link rates).
